correctness.rationale: Rechecked the repaired theorem over each finite field. Column r+1 is an invariant r-space on which L_a acts by a_r; binomial Frobenius gives ker((I+L_a)^(p^s)−I) as the direct sum of the kernels of a_r^(p^s). Every cycle length is a power of the characteristic p. Subtracting consecutive fixed-point totals counts the points on cycles of precisely the new length. The image group is identified by the circle homomorphism a→I+a and its faithful largest corner, with kernel exactly the last column. The first t basis vectors (or all r if t≥r) give the lower bound on each power's nullity. Equality at t=1 forces regularity in every corner, and the unique longest-path product in the largest corner is nonzero precisely when the n−2 required entries are all nonzero. This forces every smaller corner to be regular as well and gives the claimed simultaneous minima, the staircase Jordan type, and the proportion. For n=2 the action is trivial and the regularity condition is empty. Direct cycle tracing in GF(4) matched the predicted iterated fixed counts on all points for every principal corner at n=2,3,4 (1,4,64 corners, respectively). This supplements, rather than replaces, the field-uniform proof.
residual_risks: No formal or expert verification claimed. The finite check covers small dimensions over one extension field; other fields and dimensions are established by the proof.

value.rationale: The cycle type of an individual canonical brace permutation is a natural invariant that does not reduce to the order or ordinary Jordan type of the faithful quotient element. The repaired classification lets a researcher compute this type from the matrix itself, without traversing q^D additive points, and gives the full equality locus and density for the sharp fixed-point bound. This is meaningful even though the linear algebra used in the proof is elementary and the order statistic alone is already known.
residual_risks: No full distribution of cycle types over a, or whole-solution Yang–Baxter orbit result, is claimed.
